thread:
maria: Heads-up — saw a customer report where fncall rejections were showing up as usage on the fallback model route. Looks like quota was charged to the wrong route.
aj: ugh, that's bad. Do we have a repro?
maria: yes, small repro. Sequence: primary model returns fncall with invalid schema -> validation rejects -> router falls back to smaller model -> request succeeds. Telemetry shows only the successful route in the invoicing pipeline.
sasha: is the validation failure event emitted before routing decision? I thought we tag route earlier.
oliver: currently the router decides route at dispatch time but we only attach final route_id to the billing/event record. Validation errors are emitted to logs but not wired into the billing envelope.
kevin: that means cost/latency dashboards attribute cost to fallback, skewing per-route SLOs and quota usage. We should record an ordered list of route events (attempted -> reject -> fallback) not just final.
maria: agree. Customer is confused because their Dedicated capacity shows extra cost on the cheap fallback. They're asking for an audit trail.
aj: quick mitigation — can we add a tag to the billing emit like "attempted_route=" when validation reject happens so we at least capture the failed attempt?
sasha: short-term that seems ok. Long-term we probably want an event model change: include attempted_routes: [] and final_route in the telemetry envelope. That is a schema change though.
oliver: schema changes are fine but need careful rollout. Console dashboards and billing pipeline consumers will break if they expect route_id string.
kevin: we can keep final_route as before and add attempted_routes as optional array. Backcompat if consumers ignore new field.
maria: how about sampling? We'll be emitting more data for every reject. We should sample validation failures at 100% for now, but emit attempted_routes at 10% globally while we iterate.
aj: we already have sampling knobs in ingest. Could toggle via runtime flag.
console-bot: dashboard alert created: "fncall-route-misattrib-1793332468" — assigned to @eng-platform.
sasha: ownership question: who wires attempted_route into the billing envelope? Router (eng-runtime) or billing transform (eng-platform)?
oliver: router has the contextual info at the time of reject. It's simplest for router to emit an intermediate event (validation_reject) with attempted_route and reject_reason, and the billing transform can correlate by request id.
kevin: correlation only works if request ids are stable across retries/fallbacks — are they?
aj: currently fallback reuses the same top-level request_id, but the microservices sometimes generate new sub-ids. We need to standardize and ensure the envelope includes request_id and span ids.
maria: action items then: 1) router emits validation_reject event with attempted_route + schema_error_code, 2) billing pipeline starts ingesting validation_reject and appends attempted_routes to billing envelope when present, 3) console team adds new column "attempted routes" to route cost dashboard and adds an aggregation for reject_count.
sasha: timeline?
oliver: can do router emit in a patch this week, gated behind a feature flag. Billing ingest change requires a small transform (1-2 days) and will be behind a migration flag. Dashboard change is console work (3 days).
kevin: agree on feature flags and a canary rollout to avoid noisy spikes. We should also add an alert on any sudden increase in attempted != final ratio > 2%.
aj: question: do we expose schema_error_code to customers? Might leak internal names. Maybe map to public error classes (validation_bad_shape, validation_missing_required).
maria: yes map to hygiene-friendly error classes. Put mapping table in docs.
sasha: one more UX ask — when a user inspects a request in the console, show the timeline: attempted route, validation message, fallback decision, final route, and cost. That will help root cause.
console-bot: created ticket CONS-412 to surface request timeline in request inspector.
maria: I'll open a PR for the router event emit with feature flag. Tagging @oliver for review.
oliver: reviewing. Also let's include a tiny example payload in the PR description: ```{\n  "request_id": "r_abc123",\n  "event": "validation_reject",\n  "attempted_route": "r1-medium",\n  "error_class": "validation_bad_shape"\n}```
kevin: we should add a non-binary guard: only emit attempted_route when validation_reject_count < 1000/min per project to protect downstream.
aj: noted. Will add rate-limiter to emit.
maria: cool. Once the pipeline respects attempted_routes, we'll backfill a week of recent rejects into a special dashboard cohort to show customers.
sasha: last: include unit tests for request_id propagation and an integration test that simulates reject + fallback and asserts billing envelope contains attempted_routes array.
maria: adding tests. I'll post PR link when ready.
deploy-bot: deploy queued for patch branch "router/emit-validation-event" — awaiting approvals.
maria: thanks all.
aj: small follow-up tomorrow on sampling thresholds.
maria: ping me in #oncall if anything spikes after canary.
summary: Discussion of misattributed billing when fncall validation rejects cause router fallbacks; agreed to emit validation_reject events, add attempted_routes to telemetry/billing envelope, use feature flags + sampling, update console to show request timeline and dashboard columns, and apply rate limits and mapping of error classes.
